overview.title: Cannons Against the Atlantic
overview.p1: The Skala de la Ville is the long fortified platform on Essaouira’s western sea walls. Brass cannons still point at the horizon; the alizé pushes hard enough to lean into. It is one of the best free viewpoints in Morocco.
overview.p2: Walk the full length for views over medina roofs, the islands and open ocean. Golden hour turns the stone warm and the water silver.
overview.p3: There is little to buy on the rampart itself — treat it as a walk between the medina lanes and Place Moulay Hassan.

food.p2: Use the Skala as a breathing space between meals, not a dining stop.

q1.question: Is there an entrance fee?
q1.answer: No — the rampart walk is free.

q2.question: Is it safe with children?
q2.answer: Yes with supervision; there are drops and strong gusts.

q3.question: How long do I need?
q3.answer: Forty-five minutes is enough; longer at sunset.

q4.question: Do I need a guide at Skala de la Ville?
q4.answer: Optional for a simple visit; useful for history and local context.

q5.question: Is Skala de la Ville suitable for families?
q5.answer: Yes with normal supervision near drops, wind or busy lanes.
